title: Introduce presubmit-lite mode and toolchain snapshotter to reduce CI churn
author: Priya Choudhary
release_notes: Adds an opt-in presubmit-lite mode that warms lint/test caches and a toolchain snapshotter that pins devcontainer/tool versions to reduce presubmit variance and speed feedback.
description:
Context and motivation: Our presubmit lanes have been a major source of noisy CI and developer friction — long lint runs, transient toolchain drift, and repeated full-test shards for small changes. This PR introduces two complementary features: (1) presubmit-lite mode, an opt-in path that runs a warm-cache light lint + targeted test shard selection for small/iterative commits, and (2) a toolchain snapshotter that records the devcontainer/tool versions used when a developer runs a local presubmit, then reuses that snapshot to stabilize fastpath CI runs. The goal is to reduce average presubmit feedback time and lower unnecessary CI resource consumption without changing the strong-of-main presubmit guarantees.

What this PR does (high level):
- Adds a presubmit-lite orchestration mode behind a feature flag and repo config: .github/presubmit-lite.yml. Teams can enable for folders with fast feedback constraints.
- Implements a lightweight lint cache warmer that pre-populates the node/rust/python linters' caches on ephemeral runners to avoid cold-start penalties.
- Adds an adaptive test-shard router: small changes (determined by path-aware heuristics and a delta token budget) are routed to targeted shards; larger changes fall back to full integration presubmit.
- Introduces toolchain snapshotter: command-line shim (tools/snapshotter) that captures and uploads a compact snapshot (tool versions, package-lock hash, devcontainer digest) as a repo artifact and a presubmit label. CI reuses snapshots to create hermetic fastpath runner images.
- Adds telemetry hooks (metrics + a compact presubmit audit log) so we can measure latency, hit-rate, and cache-warm success.

Why this is safe: The main presubmit path is unchanged; presubmit-lite is opt-in and gated by a repository config value with an allowlist. All fastpath runs include a final lightweight merge-base consistency check and a forced full presubmit for PRs touching critical paths (runtime/, infra/, release/). The snapshotter only affects the runner image used for fastpath; it does not alter build artifacts or production runtime images.

Commits (summary):
- feat(ci): presubmit-lite orchestrator and config parsing
- feat(ci): implement cache-warming helper for eslint/ruff/cargo
- feat(ci): adaptive test shard router with path heuristics
- feat(ci): tools/snapshotter CLI and upload hook
- perf(ci): use snapshot digest to seed ephemeral runner images
- test(ci): add end-to-end integration harness + unit tests for heuristics
- docs: presubmit-lite README and ops playbook

Files changed (high level):
- .github/presubmit-lite.yml - new opt-in config
- .github/workflows/presubmit-lite.yml - presubmit-lite workflow that reuses existing actions with warmers
- tools/snapshotter/* - CLI shim (Go) that captures toolchain state and uploads artifact
- infra/runner-seed/seed-image-helpers.sh - small helper to apply snapshot to runner bootstrap
- ci/warmers/{lint_warmer.rs,lint_warmer.py} - language-specific cache warmers
- ci/shard-router/*.ts - router logic and heuristic tests
- docs/ops/presubmit-lite.md - rollout and troubleshooting

Testing and CI:
- Local unit tests added for router heuristics and snapshot parsing.
- Integration test in a lightweight matrix (node/python/rust) that validates end-to-end: snapshot capture -> seeded runner -> warm-cache -> targeted shard selection.
- CI initially flaked on the Rust warmer due to a path race in cache initialization (see reviews). Fixed by adding a temp directory lock and retry logic.
- Final CI status: all checks passed (lint, unit, integration, e2e matrix). Full details available in the checks summary.

Review conversation (high level):
- Ethan Morales (review): "Nice reduction in complexity compared to earlier proposal. Two asks: tighten the allowlist semantics and add an opt-out label for the PR UI so reviewers can force a full presubmit. Also can we make the snapshot upload size limit explicit?"
- Priya (author reply): "Addressed: added allowlist semantics to .github/presubmit-lite.yml and implemented a PR label override (ci/force-full-presubmit). Snapshotter now enforces a 512KB compressed payload limit and will fall back to a toolchain digest-only mode if exceeded."
- Lena Park (review): "Concern: adaptive router heuristic might under-approx small-but-impactful changes (e.g., proto changes). Suggest explicit file pattern blockers."
- Priya: "Added blocker patterns for runtime/, models/, schema/ and a final merge-base check. Documentation updated with examples."
- Omar Haddad (review): "Telemetry looks good but add a simple dashboard query for median presubmit latency and cache-warm hit rate."
- Priya: "Added metrics and a Grafana panel link in ops docs; will follow up with dashboards in infra repo."
- Approvals: Ethan/Merged after a squash-and-merge once CI green.

Migration and rollout plan (ops notes):
- Feature is opt-in. Teams enable by adding .github/presubmit-lite.yml to their repo root and toggling the allowlist.
- Pilot with SDKs (redwood-sdk-python and redwood-sdk-typescript) for two weeks. Measure: 40% reduction in median presubmit latency and 25% fewer full-run CI hours.
- After pilot, default enable for non-runtime repos with a coordinated announcement and training doc.

Known limitations and follow-ups (todo):
- Snapshotter currently records package-lock yarn.lock and cargo.lock hashes; we plan to extend to Dockerfile hashes for container toolchains.
- Heuristics will be refined after we have more telemetry — follow-up ENG tasks created (ENG-2160).
- We observed occasional checksum mismatches for devcontainer digests on older runner images; infra ticket created (ENG-2161).

Merge details:
- Merge method: squash and merge
- Squash title: "presubmit: add presubmit-lite orchestrator + toolchain snapshotter"
- Merged by: Ethan Morales on 2026-02-20

If you want to test locally:
- ./tools/snapshotter capture --out ./snapshot.json
- ./tools/snapshotter upload --file ./snapshot.json --repo redwood --pr 1234
- Run the lightweight workflow using the presubmit-lite label or by committing .github/presubmit-lite.yml with your allowlist entry.

Contact: Priya Choudhary (author) for rollout questions and infra follow-ups.
